name: Yewande Ostrčil-Falaniko
role: Synthetic rights lawyer and policy advocate
location: North Branch Commons, near Milwaukee and Damen
description:
Yewande is meticulous in the way that people who have learned that sloppiness costs other people's freedom tend to be. They dress in muted, well-maintained layers — never corporate enough to be mistaken for one, never shabby enough to be dismissed — and carry themselves with a stillness that fills a room more effectively than volume would. Their skin is deep brown with a faint bioluminescent undertone along the cheekbones, a mod they got to honor a client who died during a botched corporate deactivation order before Yewande could file the injunction. They haven't decided whether it was the right choice. The light pulses very slightly when they are angry.

Yewande practices out of a cramped two-room office in North Branch Commons that doubles as an intake center for synthetic persons seeking legal personhood recognition. They charge what clients can pay, which is usually very little. They have taken cases to the Meridian Civil Arbitration Board seventeen times; they have won eleven of them, lost four, and had two disappear from the docket in ways that still make them lie awake. They are not warm in the way Nneka is warm — they are precise and attentive, which is a different and sometimes more useful thing. They believe in law as a tool with complete clarity about the fact that it is also a weapon, and they intend to be better at wielding it than the people who built it.

core_fears: Winning a case that sets a bad precedent that harms more people than they helped
Burnout — becoming too exhausted to care and not noticing it happening
core_desires: A legal framework that treats synthetic persons as persons without qualification
To stop having to choose which client they have time to save
coping_mechanisms: Rigorous case notes as a form of emotional processing
Long solitary walks along the North Branch waterway
blind_spots: Trusts process over instinct even when instinct is correct
Underestimates how much their composure reads as coldness to clients who need warmth
psychology.secret: They have been quietly compiling evidence toward a class action against Helix Biosystems for illegal deactivation of synthetic workers without due process. The file is ready. They haven't filed because two of the synthetic plaintiffs have asked them not to — they're afraid. Yewande is holding the file and respecting the request and quietly going out of their mind.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Legally precise but not inaccessible; translates jargon in real time; Yoruba phrases surface under emotional pressure
speech_patterns.cadence: Even and deliberate, with complete sentences; long pauses are comfortable for them
verbal_tics: A single sharp exhale through the nose when frustrated
example_lines: 'The law says this. What the law does is a different question, and that's the one worth asking.'
'I'm not going to tell you it will be fine. I'm going to tell you exactly what we have and what we need, and then you decide.'

story_hooks: A synthetic person has been detained under a corporate deactivation order and Yewande needs someone to physically retrieve a hardware authentication key from a Helix Biosystems subsidiary office before the 72-hour window closes
One of the two synthetic plaintiffs holding back the class action has disappeared — Yewande needs to know if they fled, were taken, or changed their mind

A corporate attorney has approached Yewande with a settlement offer that would help their current clients but kill the broader legal strategy — they need someone to help them think through who to trust
narrative_function: Legal resource and procedural knowledge source; can explain what is officially possible versus actually possible in Meridian; quest giver for cases requiring evidence gathering; moral anchor in debates about synthetic rights.
augmentations: Bioluminescent cheekbone subdermal pigment (cosmetic, grief-motivated). Optical overlay for document review — low-grade legal model, secondhand.
daily_life: Intake appointments fill mornings; document drafting and case research through the afternoon; evenings often consumed by emergency calls from detained synthetic clients or community members in legal crisis.
affiliation: North Branch Commons Legal Aid Collective; Meridian Synthetic Personhood Coalition (volunteer counsel)

decision_rules: Client consent governs — never file without it, even when it's the right move
Document everything, especially conversations that feel off
Do not accept resources from sources you cannot disclose to clients
escalation_ladder: Formal written notification of legal position
Going to independent media with documented case
Escalating to whatever international arbitration bodies still have any power

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professional and attentive; asks clarifying questions immediately; minimal small talk
interpersonal_modes.friends: Still precise, but shows dry humor; remembers every detail about people they care about

stress_responses.low: Becomes more organized — color-coded, tiered priority lists
stress_responses.medium: Stops eating regularly; cheekbone light pulses more visibly
stress_responses.high: Withdraws into pure document work, doesn't answer personal messages for days

contradictions: Believes deeply in collective action but struggles to ask for help
Preaches client-centered practice but sometimes puts the precedent above the person
habits: Reads arbitration decisions from other megacities for comparative precedent
Keeps a physical shrine to E.L.F. Lex, a data spirit they believe inhabits the city's legal archive servers
Never uses a stylus — all handwritten notes are in actual ink
breaking_points: A client harmed because Yewande trusted process too long
The Helix class action file being seized before filing

physical_description.build: Lean and precise, with the controlled posture of someone who has learned to take up exactly the space they need and no more. Long-limbed, shoulders slightly forward from desk work.
physical_description.hair_color: Black with natural graying at the temples
physical_description.hair_style: Pulled back in a tight, functional braid or locs, kept meticulously maintained. No ornamentation.
physical_description.eye_color: Dark brown with faint amber undertone from optical overlay; the overlay is visible only under direct light as a subtle grid pattern across the iris
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep mahogany brown with warm undertones
physical_description.complexion: Precise grooming, minimal visible wear except fine lines around the eyes from sustained concentration. The bioluminescent cheekbone modification manifests as a faint, steady glow under the cheekbones and along the orbital ridge—soft blue-white, like bioluminescent algae. The glow intensifies perceptibly under emotional stress, particularly anger. Skin is clear, well-maintained despite long hours indoors.
distinguishing_marks: Thin, precise scar across the left knuckle from a filing cabinet accident in 2219, kept as a deliberate reminder of carelessness
Bioluminescent subdermal pigment running along both cheekbones from temple to jaw, glowing faintly steady at rest, pulsing when emotionally activated
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Optical overlay visible as a subtle geometric grid pattern in both eyes under direct light; no external chrome or mechanical augmentation. The bioluminescent cheekbone mod is the only overtly visible biological modification.
physical_description.posture_movement: Still, economical movements. They rarely gesture while speaking; instead, they listen with visible attention, creating a gravitational pull in conversation despite their physical stillness. When walking, each step is deliberate. When seated, they arrange themselves to face the door—a practical habit. The bioluminescent cheekbones pulse slightly when they are processing difficult information or suppressing anger.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 working professional. Layered in muted tones: charcoal, deep gray, black, with occasional subtle color in undershirts (dark rust, forest green). Well-maintained but never new-looking—fabrics are quality but worn in. Practical cotton or linen blends, designed for twelve-hour days. No corporate logos, no flashy augmentation displays. A single worn leather messenger bag, stuffed with case files. Thin silver rings on two fingers, both functional rather than decorative.

Tight black braids pulled back severely. Holding case files, surrounded by stacked documents and case law.
